one_line: Consent and scoped execution for browser-agent changes across live sites.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect live site state, negotiate supported settings, preview exact changes, pause for page approval, then apply scoped changes with receipts and undo handled by the person.
leverage_rationale: The product's core value is shared page-local state, strict schemas, capability negotiation, approval gating, state hashes, locks, expiry, and scoped receipts; generic UI-driving agents cannot reliably reproduce this contract.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes seven page tools, exact preview IDs, session/expiry/state-hash checks, protected locks, and refusal of unsupported requests.
Frame sheets visibly show tool/permission surfaces, proposed changes, approval controls, and risk areas.
About text describes six origins with different supported subsets and explicit human ownership of authority-changing actions.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually coherent cross-surface evidence and a detailed end-to-end consent workflow, with deterministic tests claimed for forged approval, stale previews, lock conflicts, and unsafe undo.
execution_evidence: 92-second demo transcript covers inspect, preview, approval, apply, refusal, receipts, and the Account Custodian example.
Frame sheets show dark and light workflow states with tool lists, proposed actions, approval, and status/result areas.
Devpost screenshot shows a resident-permit adaptation contract and human approval boundary.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real high-stakes problem: making browser agents useful without handing them broad authority, especially for credentials, permits, and account access.
impact_evidence: About text names account cleanup, permit adaptation, least privilege, prompt injection, fake authority, and dark-pattern traps.
The demo keeps approval and undo outside the agent for authority-changing operations.
The product spans accessibility-like form adaptation and account-security workflows.
creativity_rationale: The six-origin passport and negotiation/preview/approval contract is a memorable, ambitious interaction model rather than a conventional agent wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Product is framed as a third option between no access and broad click authority.
Cross-site capability negotiation and minimized enum-only interaction profiles are an original synthesis.
Gauntlet and Account Custodian extend the concept beyond a single demo screen.
usability_note: Strong visible separation between proposal, human approval, execution, receipts, and refusal; dense governance UI may require learning.
red_flags: Most visual text is small in contact sheets; final concrete account-cleanup receipt is not fully legible.
standouts: Human-owned approval and undo are enforced as product boundaries, not just copy.
Evidence covers multiple origins and adversarial safety cases.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with strong, unusually specific evidence of a real governance contract.

one_line: Agent-assisted surplus-food discovery and comparison with human checkout confirmation.
what_it_does: Finds and ranks discounted rescue packs, compares price/savings/pickup/neighborhood, and prepares checkout while leaving reservation and payment to the human.
leverage_rationale: Typed marketplace tools make constrained discovery and comparison more reliable than browsing, but a general agent could achieve much of the same flow with friction.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheet visibly labels find_rescue_packs and compare_rescue_packs calls and shows two resulting packs.
The product exposes purpose-built tools for constraints and preparation.
Checkout stops at a clearly labeled human confirmation boundary.
execution_rationale: The packet demonstrates a coherent marketplace-to-comparison-to-checkout path, though the flow stops before reservation and has no submitted video.
execution_evidence: Frames show live catalog, two available packs, comparison, and selection modal.
Devpost screenshot shows concrete sellers, prices, availability, pickup windows, and neighborhoods.
Annotations explicitly state demo inventory only and nothing submitted.
impact_rationale: It directly serves consumers seeking cheaper food and businesses trying to recover value from same-day surplus, with credible waste-reduction value.
impact_evidence: About text identifies surplus-food waste and affordability as the paired problem.
Listings visibly show discounted rescue packs and pickup details.
Human-controlled checkout avoids accidental reservations or payment.
creativity_rationale: Surplus-food rescue is an established marketplace category, but the agent-first constrained compare-and-prepare workflow is a fresh and appropriate angle.
creativity_evidence: Purpose-built find/compare/prepare tools are integrated into the marketplace.
The demo uses a Spanish/Uruguay context and preserves a consequential-action boundary.
usability_note: Clear cards, comparison, and checkout boundary; no-login demo is approachable.
red_flags: No video submission; evidence is annotated contact sheets and packaging screenshot.
No actual reservation or payment is demonstrated.
standouts: Explicit tool-call-to-UI-update evidence is legible in the contact sheet.
advance_reason: Credible, useful marketplace workflow with clear WebMCP evidence and real niche impact.

one_line: Human-supervised production planning for scenes, shots, budgets, and schedules.
what_it_does: Provides a workspace to create film projects, add scenes, generate shot plans, estimate and optimize budgets, and create shooting schedules through agent tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can keep interconnected production state consistent, but the packet does not establish that a general agent could not operate the same dashboard with friction.

execution_rationale: The dashboard appears coherent and scoped, but there is no submitted video and no end-to-end interaction evidence beyond a static Devpost capture.

About text enumerates create, generate, estimate, optimize, approve, and schedule workflow.

impact_evidence: About text identifies disconnected film-production planning tasks.

creativity_rationale: AI-assisted film-production planning is a competent domain application with a useful human-in-the-loop angle, but the interaction model is not especially novel from the evidence.
creativity_evidence: Combines production planning surfaces with an agent activity panel.
No video evidence to establish deeper originality.
usability_note: Dashboard hierarchy is understandable, though end-to-end usability is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or video transcript; evidence is primarily one Devpost screenshot and prose claims.
Access model and live tool behavior are unclear.
standouts: Clear domain-specific consolidation of core production planning tasks.
advance_reason: Potentially useful, but the packet lacks enough execution and WebMCP evidence for advancement.

one_line: Clinician agent tools with a human click before any patient-care mutation.
what_it_does: Exposes clinic queue, chart, and prescription workflows as structured tools, while requiring human confirmation for actions that write to or affect patient care.
leverage_rationale: Page-local signed-in clinical state and explicit human gating make structured agent assistance materially safer and more reliable than generic UI automation in a high-stakes setting.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and screenshot claim 20 WebMCP tools, four surfaces, and one click before anything is written.
Visible screen says the agent stops and waits before recording vitals, with Decline/Record controls.
About text explains that prescriptions, vitals, and queue moves cannot be autonomously committed.
execution_rationale: The product concept and approval state are coherent, but no video is submitted and the packet does not demonstrate a complete clinical workflow beyond the approval screen.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows Henry Sutton vitals and agent waiting for human confirmation.
Frame sheet shows clinic screens and conversational intake, though exact tool traces are illegible.
About text provides a detailed rationale and surface inventory.
impact_rationale: Clinicians face real documentation and intake burden, while mistakes in patient charts and prescriptions are consequential; human-controlled agent assistance has substantial credible value.
impact_evidence: Author describes clinical documentation, intake compression, and missed red flags as the target problem.
Visible workflow records vitals only after human confirmation.
Conversational intake in a patient’s own language is shown as an accessibility benefit.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native structured tools and a hard approval boundary to outpatient clinical care is ambitious and memorable, especially with conversational multilingual intake.
creativity_evidence: The product treats the dangerous act-first pattern as the central design problem.
Combines queue/charts/prescriptions with clinician approval and natural-language intake.
usability_note: The single explicit confirmation step is clear; clinical workflows would need careful operational validation.
red_flags: No submitted video; contact sheet text and tool names are not legible.
Clinical safety claims are demonstrated at prototype level only.
standouts: High-stakes human-in-the-loop boundary is concrete and visible.
advance_reason: High-impact, well-motivated clinical safety workflow with strong evidence of the central approval interaction.

one_line: An agent-native gallery that guides shared, interactive art exploration.
what_it_does: Lets an agent direct camera focus, illuminate hidden brushstrokes, and lead tours while a person explores digital exhibits.
leverage_rationale: Agent-directed camera, lighting, and tour state can create a genuinely collaborative gallery experience not well represented by ordinary browser clicking, though evidence is mostly promotional.
leverage_evidence: Pitch specifies camera focus, hidden-brushstroke illumination, and agent-led tours.
Devpost packaging identifies a complete W3C WebMCP implementation across 12 tools.
No frame sheets were submitted to verify live operation.
execution_rationale: The concept and visual packaging are coherent, but no frame sheets, video transcript, or readable live workflow evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows the branded gallery project and demo video thumbnail.
About text describes intended gallery interactions but does not demonstrate completion.
impact_rationale: Visitors, learners, galleries, and docents have a credible use for guided, accessible art exploration, though the packet does not show effectiveness.
impact_evidence: About text identifies personal art-discovery difficulty and real-world gallery/docent use.

creativity_rationale: Using an agent as a spatial gallery guide and lighting/camera director is a notably original interaction model with artistic ambition.
creativity_evidence: Agent changes the presentation and discovery context of artworks, not merely text captions.
The concept is explicitly designed around joint human-agent exploration.
usability_note: The gallery metaphor is clear, but operation and accessibility cannot be assessed from packaging alone.

advance_reason: Creative concept is promising, but execution and WebMCP evidence are too thin for advancement.

one_line: Collaborative browser-based live visual engine and routing graph for events.
what_it_does: Combines a shared real-time visual node graph, WebRTC camera sources, GPU-rendered outputs, and agent assistance for live-event visual production.
leverage_rationale: Shared graph state, media routing, multiple operators, and agent assistance make structured state access materially valuable beyond UI driving for a live production system.
leverage_evidence: About text describes Yjs/CRDT shared graph, cursor presence, camera/display nodes, and agent creation/management.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows a node-based visual production interface.
Frame sheets show changing visual node/output states, but exact tool names are illegible.
execution_rationale: The product scope is ambitious and the visual frames show a functioning-looking node workspace with evolving outputs, though no transcript or clear end-to-end live routing result is provided.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show node/tile workflows and accumulating visual outputs.
About text specifies browser, WebGPU, WebRTC, CRDT, camera, and display workflows.
Devpost screenshot shows the visual engine demo presentation.
impact_rationale: Live-event operators have real routing, hardware, collaboration, and failure-diagnosis burdens; a browser-native shared graph could be valuable to that niche audience.
impact_evidence: About text explains current TouchDesigner/Resolume hardware and cabling pain points.
Product supports phones as camera sources and laptops as outputs through links.
creativity_rationale: Turning browsers, phones, operators, displays, and media streams into a shared live visual graph is a highly ambitious and memorable synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Browser nodes can become camera sources or local GPU displays.
CRDT collaboration and matrix-style routing target a traditionally hardware-bound workflow.
Combines Figma-like collaboration with TouchDesigner-like visual processing.
usability_note: The node-graph metaphor is powerful but complex; reliable live-event operation is not fully demonstrated.
red_flags: Tool invocation details and live WebRTC routing are not legible in the supplied frames.
standouts: Strong browser-native replacement thesis for hardware-heavy live visuals.
Shared state and presence are central rather than decorative.
advance_reason: Ambitious, original creative infrastructure with credible product evidence and meaningful structured-state leverage.

one_line: A runtime that preserves intent and verifies agent recovery of failed workflows.
what_it_does: Captures user intent, partial progress, failures, capabilities, policies, and invariants so an agent can replan unfinished workflows with deterministic verification at every step.
leverage_rationale: The product changes agent execution from ad hoc clicking into verified, stateful recovery with application-defined legal actions and invariants; generic UI automation cannot provide comparable guarantees.
leverage_evidence: About text defines preserved intent, succeeded steps, failure evidence, capabilities, policies, and invariants.
Pitch and screenshot show an engineering repair pipeline with validation envelope, reproducer, regression assertion, and change boundary.
Every action is claimed to be verified by deterministic application code.
execution_rationale: The concept and pipeline surfaces are coherent, but the frame sheets show repeated near-identical states and do not clearly demonstrate a completed recovery or concrete final repair.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show agent console/browser workflow and apparent validation markers.
Devpost screenshot shows named repair-pipeline stages.
About text describes a concrete demo but the submitted visual evidence is not legible enough to verify its endpoint.
impact_rationale: Recovering user intent after failures is a real developer and workflow problem, with value in reducing lost work while constraining unsafe mutation.
impact_evidence: About text identifies lost intention, partial progress, and safe next steps as the gap.
The system preserves evidence and policies rather than granting unrestricted access.
creativity_rationale: Treating unfinished workflows as first-class recoverable state and combining agent replanning with deterministic verification is a fresh, ambitious developer-tool concept.
creativity_evidence: Core framing is developers define legal actions while agents discover workable sequences.
Failure evidence, invariants, and validation envelopes are integrated into the runtime model.
usability_note: The staged repair pipeline is conceptually clear but visually dense and not proven end-to-end.
red_flags: Frames are repetitive and low resolution; exact recovered workflow and final output are not readable.
standouts: Strong distinction between agent discovery and deterministic authority.
First-class preservation of intent is a useful product primitive.
advance_reason: Meaningful agent-infrastructure idea with strong conceptual leverage, despite incomplete visual endpoint evidence.

leverage_rationale: Typed card and layout operations produce structured, editable shared state more reliably than an agent typing prose, but a general agent could perform much of the same work with friction.

one_line: Conversational, parametric Konkan-house design for homeowners and contractors.

execution_evidence: Transcript includes measured proposal, user approval, applied change, duplicated floor, roof wall, and later staircase request.

impact_evidence: About text explains the regional housing-grant and architect-access gap.

The workflow makes design visible before construction.

one_line: Shared brick CAD where agents and people edit the same validated 3D model.
what_it_does: Provides catalog search, real modeled parts, placement, connection/collision checks, protected regions, revision-aware preflight, undo, and structured agent editing through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes exact live CAD state, selections, revisions, connectors, validation summaries, and a preflight path shared with human edits; screenshot-driving cannot comparably guarantee physically coherent operations.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly contrasts structured state with screenshots and lists revision, protected regions, collision, connectivity, and constraints checks.
Agent edits run through the same connector logic, validation, and undo history as manual edits.
Catalog results distinguish placeable, modeled, and cataloged parts so the agent selects valid geometry.
execution_rationale: The 179-second demo describes and visually shows catalog search, model editing, agent transformations, live inspection, preflight ghost result, validation, and undo; the workflow is coherent and complete for a CAD prototype.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers 80,000 indexed identities, 900 modeled parts, gothic transformation, orbit inspection, tool calls, preflight, and ghost result.
Frame sheets show iterative 3D/node-like build states and outputs.
Devpost screenshot shows a branded CAD product and live model presentation.
impact_rationale: Builders, LEGO designers, educators, and creative hobbyists gain a real editable design partner that handles repetitive geometry while preserving human iteration.
impact_evidence: About text names real parts, connectors, editable models, manual and agent workflows.
The product addresses the gap between text/image AI and reconstructing physically valid geometry by hand.
Visible demo shows a six-story build and transformation workflow.
creativity_rationale: The shared-consequence model—human and agent manipulating one physically validated brick object—is a memorable and deeply pursued interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human share the same model, selection, revision, validation, and undo state.
The system applies CAD-kernel checks to an expressive creative building task.
Catalog scale and real geometry make the concept more than a toy mockup.
usability_note: Manual drag/orbit and agent operations converge on one validated model with undo; catalog breadth may add complexity.
red_flags: Demo_alive is unknown in packet, so live-host verification is unavailable.

standouts: Best evidence of structured shared state and validation changing what an agent can safely do.
Agent edits are visible as inspectable ghost/preflight results rather than opaque mutations.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage, strong end-to-end evidence, and an unusually compelling shared creative/CAD workflow.
